text: The user plans to start learning about deep learning and asked for online resources or courses for beginners. As of 17 November 2022 the user has just completed an undergraduate degree in computer science and has a solid foundation in CS concepts.

The assistant recommended beginner deep learning courses: Andrew Ng's Deep Learning Specialization on Coursera (5 courses), Deep Learning by Google on Coursera (3 courses), Deep Learning A-Z on Udemy, and Deep Learning with Python on DataCamp.

The assistant also recommended beginner deep learning resources: Kaggle, the TensorFlow Tutorials on TensorFlow.org, the free online Deep Learning Book by Ian Goodfellow, Yoshua Bengio and Aaron Courville, and the deeplearning.ai blog run by Andrew Ng.

The assistant advised deep learning beginners to start with fundamentals such as neural networks, backpropagation and optimisation techniques, practise with projects in image classification, object detection or NLP, join communities such as r/MachineLearning and r/DeepLearning, and read research papers.

The user wants to explore natural language processing and asked for NLP resources or courses that fit their CS background and their recent experience with an NLP research paper, in the session dated 17 November 2022.

The assistant recommended NLP courses: Natural Language Processing with Deep Learning by Prof. Christopher Manning on Stanford Online, an NLP course from University of Colorado Boulder on Coursera, Deep Learning for Natural Language Processing from University of Oxford on edX, and Natural Language Processing with Python and NLTK on DataCamp.

The assistant recommended NLP reading resources: the free NLTK Book by Steven Bird, Ewan Klein and Edward Loper, the spaCy documentation at spacy.io, the Stanford Natural Language Processing Group website, and the ACL Anthology digital archive of Association for Computational Linguistics papers.
The user wants to explore transformers and attention mechanisms and asked for resources or tutorials that give a detailed explanation of these concepts in the context of NLP.

The assistant recommended transformer tutorials: Jay Alammar's blog series The Transformer Family, the Distill interactive article Attention Is All You Need, the TensorFlow tutorial on a Transformer model for language translation, and the Machine Learning Mastery tutorial on attention mechanisms in NLP.

The assistant listed foundational transformer and attention papers: Vaswani et al. (2017) Attention Is All You Need, Devlin et al. (2019) on BERT, and Dosovitskiy et al. (2020) An Image is Worth 16x16 Words on Transformers for image recognition.

The assistant recommended transformer videos and implementations: the 3Blue1Brown animated video Transformer Model Explained, a Sentdex video on attention mechanisms in deep learning, a PyTorch tutorial implementing the Transformer, and a TensorFlow tutorial implementing BERT.

The user asked about applications of transformers and attention mechanisms in NLP tasks such as text classification, sentiment analysis and question answering, and requested resources or papers that show their effectiveness.

The assistant recommended text classification resources: the Google AI Blog post on BERT for text classification, the Hugging Face tutorial on text classification with transformers covering BERT, RoBERTa and DistilBERT, and a KDNuggets guide to fine-tuning BERT for text classification.

The assistant recommended sentiment analysis and question answering resources: an ACL 2020 paper on BERT-based sentiment analysis, a TensorFlow tutorial on sentiment analysis with transformers, the Google AI Blog post on BERT for question answering, and the Hugging Face tutorial on question answering with transformers.

The assistant listed further transformer papers for these tasks: RoBERTa (Li et al., 2019), DistilBERT (Sanh et al., 2019) and XLNet (Yang et al., 2020), along with the Hugging Face Transformers library, TensorFlow Transformers and NLTK as resources.

The user asked about applications of transformers and attention mechanisms in language translation, text generation and dialogue systems, and requested resources or papers that showcase their effectiveness in these areas.

The assistant recommended language translation papers: Vaswani et al. (2017) The Transformer Model for Machine Translation, Lample et al. (2019) on bilingual transformers for machine translation, and Zhou et al. (2020) on multi-task learning for machine translation with transformers.

The assistant recommended text generation papers: Dai et al. (2019) on Transformer-XL, Wang et al. (2020) on BERT-based text generation, and Krause et al. (2020) on controllable text generation with transformers.

The assistant recommended dialogue system papers: Chen et al. (2020) on transformer-based dialogue systems, Zhang et al. (2020) on dialogue generation with transformers, and Li et al. (2020) on multi-turn dialogue response generation with transformers.

The assistant listed additional general papers: T5 by Raffel et al. (2020), BART by Lewis et al. (2020), and Long-Range Arena by Tay et al. (2020), a benchmark for evaluating efficient transformers on long-range dependencies.

The user asked about applications of transformers and attention mechanisms in computer vision, particularly image classification, object detection and image generation, and requested resources or papers that show their effectiveness.

The assistant recommended image classification papers: Vision Transformers (ViT) by Dosovitskiy et al. (2020), Swin Transformer by Liu et al. (2021), and Transformer-based image classification with self-attention by Wang et al. (2020).

The assistant recommended object detection and image generation papers: DETR by Carion et al. (2020), Deformable DETR by Zhu et al. (2020), TransGAN by Jiang et al. (2020) for image generation, and StyleSwin by Chen et al. (2021).

The assistant listed further computer vision resources: transformer papers on image segmentation (Chen et al., 2020), image denoising (Zhang et al., 2020) and image compression (Li et al., 2020), plus PyTorch Vision Transformers, TensorFlow Vision Transformers and OpenCV.
As of 15 May 2023 the user has just submitted their master's thesis in computer science and wants recommendations on NLP research papers to stay up to date with the latest developments in the field.

The assistant recommended language model and transformer papers: BERT by Devlin et al. (2019), RoBERTa by Liu et al. (2019), and Transformer-XL by Dai et al. (2019), which lets transformers handle longer input sequences.

The assistant recommended text classification and sentiment papers: Deep Emotional Speech by Wang et al. (2020) on emotional information in speech recognition and sentiment analysis, and Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis with Graph Attention Networks by Huang et al. (2020).

The assistant recommended question answering and dialogue papers: BERT-based Question Answering on SQuAD 2.0 by Wang et al. (2019), and DialoGLUE by Mehri et al. (2020), a natural language understanding benchmark for task-oriented dialogue.

The assistant recommended explainability and multilingual papers: Attention is not Explanation by Jain et al. (2019), LIME by Ribeiro et al. (2016), Multimodal Fusion with Deep Neural Networks for Multimodal Sentiment Analysis by Kim et al. (2020), and Multilingual BERT: A Case Study for Arabic by Antoun et al. (2020).

The assistant recommended two further papers on neural network behaviour: The Lottery Ticket Hypothesis by Frankle et al. (2019) and Adversarial Examples Are Not Bugs, They Are Features by Ilyas et al. (2019).

The assistant suggested staying current in NLP by following the NLP Subreddit, the ACL Blog, the NAACL Blog, NLP News and the AI Alignment Forum, and by taking courses such as Stanford CS224D, CS230 and a NAACL tutorial on transformers.
The user said they are particularly interested in the Language Models and Transformers section and asked about applications of BERT in industry settings, such as chatbots or virtual assistants.

The assistant described BERT uses in chatbots, including conversational understanding, intent detection, entity recognition and response generation, and cited examples such as IBM Watson Assistant, Medibio's health chatbot, Capital One's Eno, Google Duplex, Microsoft Zo and Amazon Alexa.

The assistant listed challenges for BERT-based chatbots: domain adaptation when data is limited or terminology is unique, explainability of decisions, and multimodal interaction combining voice, text and vision.
The user is exploring BERT-based models for sentiment analysis of customer feedback and asked how BERT can be fine-tuned for sentiment analysis and which datasets are typically used for this purpose.

The assistant gave a six-step guide to fine-tuning BERT for sentiment analysis: choose a pre-trained model, prepare labelled data, tokenise with the matching WordPiece tokenizer, convert to input IDs, attention masks, token type IDs and labels, fine-tune with Adam and cross-entropy loss, then tune hyperparameters.

The assistant listed sentiment analysis datasets: IMDB with 50,000 movie reviews, the Stanford Sentiment Treebank (SST-2) described as 10,000 movie reviews, Amazon Product Reviews, the Yelp Dataset, and custom customer feedback datasets.
The user asked how to adapt BERT for aspect-based sentiment analysis (ABSA) in customer feedback and which datasets are typically used for this purpose.

The assistant explained adapting BERT for ABSA: identify aspects using NER, POS tagging or dependency parsing, add aspect-specific tokens, build aspect masks and per-aspect sentiment labels, and use aspect-based attention and aspect-aware pooling layers.

The assistant listed ABSA datasets: Semeval-2014 with 3,000 restaurant reviews, Semeval-2015 with 1,500 laptop reviews, Amazon Product Reviews, the Yelp Dataset, and custom annotated customer feedback datasets.
The user said they want to explore BERT-based models for intent detection in customer feedback and asked how to adapt BERT for intent detection and which datasets are typically used.

The assistant described adapting BERT for intent detection: identify customer intents such as request refund or report issue, add intent-specific tokens, build intent masks and labels, and train intent identification and intent classification tasks.

The assistant listed intent detection datasets: CLINC150 with 15,000 customer feedback samples, HWU64 with 64,000 samples covering a wide range of products and services, Amazon Product Reviews, the Yelp Dataset, and custom customer feedback datasets.
The user asked how to adapt BERT for dialogue systems and which datasets are typically used for this purpose.

The assistant described adapting BERT for dialogue systems using [USER] and [SYSTEM] tokens, dialogue masks and dialogue act labels, and training for dialogue response generation and dialogue state tracking.

The assistant listed dialogue datasets: the Ubuntu Dialogue Corpus with 1 million utterances, DialogRE with 10,000 dialogues, ConvAI2 with 10,000 dialogues, DSTC with 10,000 dialogues and dialogue states, and custom customer service datasets.
As of 20 May 2023 the user is planning a fishing trip to Lake Michigan with friends and asked for tips on the best spots to catch trout.

The assistant advised trout anglers on Lake Michigan to fish near tributaries such as the St. Joseph River and Grand River in Michigan and the Milwaukee River in Wisconsin, and at structures including the Chicago Light Shipwreck, Gary Reef in Indiana and Saugatuck Reef in Michigan.

The assistant said Lake Michigan trout tend to prefer water temperatures of 40 to 55 F (4 to 13 C) and depths of 50 to 200 feet (15 to 61 metres), with spring fishing at 20 to 50 feet, summer at 50 to 150 feet, and fall in shallower water near shorelines and tributaries.

The assistant recommended harbours and piers such as Chicago's Navy Pier, Milwaukee's McKinley Marina and St. Joseph's Harbor as shelter for trout during strong winds or cold fronts, and advised checking regulations and obtaining licences before the trip.
The user said that from prior experience fishing Lake Michigan, spinner lures worked better for trout than live bait, and that on their last trip there they caught 12 largemouth bass.

The assistant recommended trout spinner lures for Lake Michigan: Rapala Original Floater or Deep Tail Dancer in silver or gold, Mepps Aglia in 1/16 to 1/4 oz in silver, gold or copper, Blue Fox Vibrax in size 1 or 2, and Rooster Tail in 1/16 to 1/4 oz in white, silver or gold.
The assistant advised varying retrieve speed, using a weighted line or downrigger for depth control, and trying steady, stop-and-go or slow sweeping actions when fishing spinners for trout.
The assistant noted that largemouth bass can be targeted on Lake Michigan with a variety of lures and techniques, and offered to provide bass tips and recommendations if the user is interested.
The user is thinking of organising a fly fishing trip to Montana or Colorado next summer, relative to the 20 May 2023 session, and asked for tips or recommendations for that trip.

The assistant recommended Montana fly fishing rivers including the Big Horn, Madison and Missouri, and Colorado fly fishing rivers including the Arkansas, Blue and South Platte, describing the Arkansas and Blue as tailwater fisheries with consistent temperatures and flows.

The assistant advised that summer is prime fly fishing time in Montana and Colorado, but spring (April to May) or fall (September to October) offers fewer crowds and more aggressive fish, and suggested dry flies such as hoppers and stimulators and nymphs such as pheasant tails and copper johns.

The assistant suggested bringing a 9-foot, 5-weight or 6-weight fly rod, booking a guide or lodge early for access to private water, wearing waders or boots with good traction, packing layers, and obtaining a fishing licence for each state visited.
The user said they are thinking of taking a class to learn more about fly fishing, especially tying their own flies, and asked for online resources or books to get started with fly tying.

The assistant recommended online fly tying resources: The Fly Fishing Academy (flyfishingacademy.com) with an online fly tying course, Fly Tying 101 (flytying101.com), The Fly Tying Forum (flytyingforum.com), and YouTube channels including Fly Tying 101, The Fly Fishing Guide and Fly Fishing the Globe.

The assistant recommended fly tying books: The Fly Tyer's Bible by Peter C. Whitlock, Fly Tying for Beginners by Mike Lawson, The Orvis Fly Tying Guide by Tom Rosenbauer, and The Fly Tier's Companion by Darrell Martin.

The assistant gave beginner fly tying tips: invest in a good vise, start with basic dry fly hackle, wet fly hackle and dubbing, practise simple patterns regularly, join a fly fishing community, and consider an online class or workshop.
The user is thinking of restocking their tackle box with size 2 hooks and chartreuse plastic worms and asked whether these are good for catching largemouth bass.

The assistant said size 2 hooks are a good all-round size for largemouth bass with soft plastics, that 1/0 or 2/0 hooks suit larger bass or bigger baits, and that chartreuse worms are effective in clearer water when bass feed on shad or other baitfish.
The assistant suggested green pumpkin, watermelon or June bug worms in murkier water or when bass are finicky, and fishing worms slowly with a sweeping motion around weed beds, rocks or sunken logs.
The user is considering taking their Shimano Curado rod to a repair shop because it has a slight crack in a guide, and asked whether to get it repaired or buy a new rod.

The assistant said a slight crack is not necessarily fatal and that the decision depends on crack severity, the rod's age and condition, the repair quote (repair is worth considering at around $20 to $50), and the user's budget and preferences.

The assistant noted that a new rod brings improved materials and features, a warranty, better customer support and better resale value, and recommended getting a professional assessment and researching new models before deciding.

As of 24 May 2023 the user reported that their Twitter follower count jumped from 420 to 540 over the past month, which the user found really encouraging, and asked for help analysing their social media performance.
The user wants to increase their online presence and drive traffic to their website through Twitter, and in the session dated 24 May 2023 said they want to optimise their social media strategy.

The user posts a mix of educational and personal content on Twitter, has been trying to post at least 5 to 7 tweets per day, has no specific content calendar, and stays consistent by responding to comments and direct messages.

The assistant suggested tracking a Twitter engagement rate of at least 2 to 3 percent, a follower growth rate of 5 to 10 percent per month, and website clicks via a URL shortener such as Bitly, and advised focusing on quality over quantity in posting.

The assistant recommended experimenting with visuals, questions or polls, behind-the-scenes content and user-generated content, and optimising the Twitter profile with a complete profile picture, header image and clear bio.

The user wants to focus on increasing their Twitter engagement rate. The assistant suggested ten tactics: asking questions, Twitter polls, engaging visuals, hosting a Twitter Chat or Q&A, humour and personality, user-generated content, timing tweets, responding to comments, influencer collaboration and a retweet-to-win contest.
The user has participated in Twitter Chats before, finds the idea of hosting a Twitter Chat or Q&A session interesting, and asked for tips on hosting a successful one.

The assistant advised pre-chat preparation for a Twitter Chat: choose a relevant topic, set a specific date and time when the audience is active, create a unique hashtag, promote the chat, and prepare open-ended questions.

The assistant advised during and after a Twitter Chat: welcome participants, ask open-ended questions, use the hashtag, thank participants, share key takeaways, follow up, analyse performance, keep answers concise, and have a plan for trolls or negative comments.
The user said they are ready to try hosting a Twitter Chat and asked for ideas on how to promote it beforehand.

The assistant gave ten promotion ideas for a Twitter Chat: tweets using the hashtag, Instagram and Facebook Stories, co-hosting with influencers, a blog post, an email newsletter, Facebook and LinkedIn groups, a Twitter poll, guest blogging, paid ads and countdown tweets.

The user noted that the assistant had mentioned the Twitter follower count jump from 420 to 540, and suggested the assistant share insights or tips on its Twitter growth strategy during the Q&A session.

The assistant replied that as a conversational AI it has no personal experiences or growth strategies, but offered general Twitter growth tips for a Q&A: consistency, engagement, content diversification, hashtag strategy, and collaboration with other accounts.
As of 24 May 2023 the user is doing well on Instagram and wants to know whether there are specific times of day that are best for posting to maximise engagement.
As of 24 May 2023 the user's Facebook follower count has remained steady at around 800, while their Facebook posts have been getting more shares and comments than usual.

The assistant gave posting times: on Instagram, peak engagement at 12 pm to 1 pm and 5 pm to 6 pm, best on Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday; on Facebook, peak at 12 pm to 3 pm, best on Thursday, Friday and Sunday. Both avoid 5 am to 7 am and 9 pm to 11 pm.

The assistant suggested the user test posting times with Instagram Insights or Facebook Page Insights, avoid overposting, use scheduling tools such as Hootsuite, Buffer or Sprout Social, and respond promptly to comments and messages.
The assistant suggested possible reasons for the rise in Facebook shares and comments: improved content quality, increased audience interest in the niche, or favourable Facebook algorithm changes.
The user said they will experiment with different posting times and asked for tips on creating engaging content for Facebook that resonates with their audience.

The assistant gave fifteen Facebook content tips, including knowing the audience through buyer personas, being authentic, using visuals, keeping captions concise, asking questions, storytelling, interactive polls and quizzes, and optimising for mobile.

The assistant listed Facebook content types that tend to perform well: short videos, listicles, behind-the-scenes content, user-generated content, how-to guides, inspirational content, humorous content and exclusive offers or promotions.

The user said their Instagram Stories get a lot of views, especially when they use the question sticker to ask followers questions, and asked for more ideas on using Stories to increase engagement and attract new followers.

The assistant suggested Instagram Story tactics: poll, quiz, chat and slider stickers, link traffic, multi-part story series, Story Highlights, influencer takeovers, exclusive deals, Story Ads, timing, user-generated content and tracking with Instagram Insights.
As of 24 May 2023 the user has been posting short videos on TikTok showcasing their hobbies and interests, and has been surprised by how quickly their TikTok follower count has grown.

The assistant gave fifteen TikTok growth tips, including identifying a niche, developing a consistent style, using catchy music, leveraging hashtags, engaging the community, collaborating with creators, using Duets, posting consistently and using TikTok Analytics.
The user said they are thinking about how to use each social media platform for its strengths, and asked for advice on growing their Facebook following, which has stayed steady at around 800.

The assistant gave ten Facebook growth tips: optimise the Page, post engaging content, engage with the audience, leverage Facebook Groups, run Facebook Ads, collaborate with influencers and other Pages, share user-generated content, host Facebook Live sessions, analyse Insights and cross-promote.
The user asked for more information on how to create and manage a Facebook Group and how to use it to attract new followers.

The assistant gave a guide to creating a Facebook Group: choose a clear name, add a profile picture and cover photo, write a detailed description, set privacy settings and add a call to action, then manage it by defining purpose, setting rules, posting engaging content, encouraging participation and moderating.

The assistant suggested attracting new members to a Facebook Group by promoting it on the Page, offering exclusive content, hosting events and webinars, collaborating with influencers, sharing user-generated content, using Live and Events, optimising for search and running a contest or giveaway.
